There's a green circle in the middle of the instructions marking a drawing of a wheel assembly. So the green circle at top left marks a physical piece (red beam), but the green circle in the instructions marks a wheel drawing. These don't match - the physical piece circled in green (red beam) is not the same as the drawing circled in green (wheel). So green doesn't mark both the same physical piece and its drawing.

Red circle: Top right, marks a gray physical piece (a hub/rim). There's also a red circle in the instructions at the bottom marking a drawing of that gray hub/rim piece. Yes! The red circle at top right shows a gray wheel hub physical piece, and the red circle in the instructions (near step 9) shows the drawing of that same gray hub piece. So red marks both a physical piece and its drawing.

Purple circle: Marks the hands holding a wheel, no drawing in purple in instructions.

Blue circle: Marks the step numbers 7 and 10 in the instructions, not physical pieces.

So the answer is red.

Let me double check the red circle in the instructions. At the bottom of the instruction sheet, near step 9, there's a red circle around a drawing of a gray hub piece. Yes, that matches the physical gray hub at top right.

Thus the answer is B.

The question asks "which of the circle colors mark a physical piece, and a drawing of that physical piece in the instructions?" So the same color must appear on both a physical piece and its drawing. Red appears on the physical gray hub and on the drawing of the gray hub. Green appears on a physical red beam and on a drawing of a wheel - mismatch. So red is correct.

Answer: B.
